subject: Readiness: Risks, 'Orange Paths', and runbook ownership
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Readiness: Risks, 'Orange Paths', and runbook ownership

Team —

With April 2 go-live on the horizon I want to surface a compact set of readiness decisions and proposed owners so we can close the loop this week. Key context: this launch has a three-tier fallback plan (green = normal, orange = degraded but serving, red = rollback). The ‘orange’ paths are the trickiest operationally and we need clear owners, a short runbook, and the canary window / rollback criteria finalized.

Two asks for today:
- Confirm owners for runbook and rollback scripts (who will apply fix/rollback in the orange case)
- Approve the canary window and the specific rollback triggers below

Proposed quick decisions:
- Canary window: Apr 2, 09:00–12:00 PT (3 hours)
- Orange triggers (examples): sustained 95th p99 latency > 600ms for > 3 minutes, error rate > 2% for 5 minutes, or token cost-per-request > 1.5x baseline for 10 minutes

Attachments: runbook_draft.md, staging-checklist.xlsx (worksheet with handoffs) — please review.

If you can reply with owners and any objections by EOD today I’ll publish an updated runbook and create the JIRA ticket linking to the rollback playbook.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Readiness: Risks, 'Orange Paths', and runbook ownership

Jonas —

Thanks for outlining. A couple of clarifying items from infra/serving side:
- Canary window OK for timing; can we set an initial traffic ramp schedule (25% -> 50% -> 100%) each step 20 minutes? That gives us quick validation points.
- For the orange fallback, propose we pin a dedicated fallback variant: rwd-small-quant (lower cost, 4GB KV) so we have an explicit model to flip to during orange. Otherwise decisions are ad-hoc.
- Need an owner for the traffic-shift script (I volunteer infra to own the traffic automation but we need someone to own the runbook decision to initiate shift).

Suggested owners:
- Traffic-shift automation: Marcus Lin (infra)
- Runbook/final doc owner: Laura (prod)
- Customer comms template: Marissa

Quick question: do we want the runbook to include the exact commandset for aws/priv infra (yes/no)? If yes, I’ll add a short appendix to the staging-checklist.xlsx.

- Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

All —

I’ll take runbook ownership and will publish runbook_v1.md by EOD. Per Marcus, infra will own traffic-shift automation; I will own the decision checklist to kick that automation. Action items and owners below:

- Runbook doc (final owner): Laura Bennett — deliver runbook_v1.md (EOD today)
- Rollback scripts & automation owner: Marcus Lin — validate traffic-shift scripts and provide a dry-run by Mar 28
- Customer comms template: Marissa Cole — draft and circulate by Mar 24
- Training & enablement slot booking: Kimberly Park — reserve 3/28 and 3/30 training slots for CS and CSMs
- Staging checklist updates (infra appendix): Marcus to add commandset to staging-checklist.xlsx

I'll include a short 'decision ladder' in runbook_v1.md that lists the exact metric thresholds and who has the authority to escalate to red/rollback. Attaching the updated runbook_v1.md (minor edits + clearer table of contents).

Please ACK owners so I can lock the doc.

Laura
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_v1.md
